resources.name: ContactPointDisposition
resources.doc:
One terminal disposition per locator. A replacement must belong to the same set and kind
and begin exactly where the old one ends, so supersession chains move strictly forward
and cannot cycle. Uniqueness makes two racing revoke/supersede attempts fail atomically.

resources.name: ContactPointVerification
resources.doc:
Verification is evidence that a locator reached who it claimed to, kept separate from
the locator so an unverified address is still a usable fact rather than a missing one.

resources.name: LocatorKind
resources.doc:
Kinds are a registry rather than an enum so an application can add `mcp` or a queue
dialect without a language change. `personal` is what keeps the two profiles apart, and
it is enforced by a rule on each of them rather than by convention.

resources.name: LocatorPurpose
resources.doc:
Purpose is a label on reachability, not a governance purpose and not a notification
preference: `billing` says which address to use for invoices, never whether the subject
agreed to receive them. Consent and preference are separate facts elsewhere.

dataClasses.name: ContactValue
dataClasses.doc:
How to reach something. Contact points reach people, endpoints reach systems.

These are two resources rather than one polymorphic locator because a data
classification is a property of a field, not of a row. One `value` column would have to
be classified once: as contact data, which sweeps webhook URLs into subject-rights
erasure that does not apply to them, or as structural, which under-classifies an email
address. Neither is acceptable, so the split is in the model.

No transport mechanics live here. A locator says where something can be reached, never
how a provider delivers to it, what retry policy applies, or whether a message was sent.
Delivery #38 and Notifications #50 own those.

resources.name: CustomerAccount
resources.doc: A Party-shaped owner: a person or organization reached through contact points.

resources.name: FieldDevice
resources.doc:
A device: also a non-Party subject, and the case that shows a locator set belongs to
whatever owns it rather than to a person.

resources.name: OutboundRoute
resources.doc:
A notification-shaped consumer. It selects an already-declared endpoint to send to and
records nothing about reachability itself: no value, no validity, no verification. This
is the shape #50 would take over this substrate, kept here as a probe so the boundary is
executable rather than asserted in prose.

resources.name: SupportService
resources.doc:
A non-Party subject. Services are reached through endpoints, never contact points,
and the rule on each profile is what enforces that rather than this fixture's intent.

classification.business: declared domain errors: served, counted separately
classification.counting: one event per logical operation; retries are attempts on the same event, never new events

info.title: @foundation-probe/reachability-consumers
info.description: Generated by forgec build; a projection of the same contracts the runtime enforces on every target.
